blocks.title: Random partitions…
blocks.content:
An *integer partition*, called also a *Young diagram*, is a weakly decreasing finite sequence $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_l)$ of positive integers $\lambda_1\geq \cdots \geq \lambda_l>0$. We also say that $\lambda$ is a partition of $|\lambda|:=\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_l$.

*Random partitions* occur in mathematics and physics in a wide variety of contexts, in particular in the Gromov--Witten and Seiberg--Witten theories, see the overview articles of Okounkov [@Okounkov2003] and Vershik [@VershikICM].

blocks.title: …and random matrices
blocks.content: Certain random partitions can be regarded as discrete counterparts of some interesting ensembles of random matrices. We shall explore this link on a particular example of random matrices called *$\beta$-ensembles* or *$\beta$-log gases* [@Forrester], i.e. the probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the density of the form $$p(x_1,\dots,x_n) =  \frac{1}{Z} e^{V(x_1)+\cdots+V(x_n)}  \prod_{i<j} |x_i - x_j|^{\beta},$$ where $V$ is some real-valued function and $Z$ is the normalization constant. blocks.title: Front matter
blocks.content:
arXiv:1704.02352v2  [math.PR]  15 May 2018
GAUSSIAN FLUCTUATIONS
OF JACK-DEFORMED RANDOM YOUNG DIAGRAMS
MACIEJ DOŁ ˛EGA AND PIOTR ´SNIADY
ABSTRACT. We introduce a large class of random Young diagrams which
can be regarded as a natural one-parameter deformation of some classi-
cal Young diagram ensembles; a deformation which is related to Jack
polynomials and Jack characters. We show that each such a random
Young diagram converges asymptotically to some limit shape and that
the ﬂuctuations around the limit are asymptotically Gaussian.

blocks.title: Random Young diagrams related to log-gases
blocks.content:
Opposite to the special cases $\beta\in\{1,2,4\}$, in the generic case of $\beta$-ensembles there seems to be no obvious unique way of defining their discrete counterparts and several alternative approaches are available, see the work of Moll [@Moll2015] as well as the work of Borodin, Gorin and Guionnet [@BorodinGorinGuionnet2015]. In the current paper we took another approach based on a deformation of the character theory of the symmetric groups.

blocks.title: Random Young diagrams related to Thoma's characters
blocks.content:
An additional motivation for considering this particular class of random Young diagrams stems from the research related to the problem of finding extremal characters of the infinite symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}(\infty)$, solved by Thoma [@Thoma1964]. Vershik and Kerov [@VershikKerov1981a] found an alternative, more conceptual proof of Thoma's result, which was based on the observation that *characters of $\mathfrak{S}(\infty)$ are in a natural bijective correspondence with certain sequences $(\lambda_1\nearrow \lambda_2\nearrow\cdots)$ of growing random Young diagrams*.

For partitions $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_k$ we define their *product* $\pi_1 \cdots \pi_k$ as their concatenation, for example $(4,3) \cdot (5,3,1)=(5,4,3,3,1)$. In this way the set of all partitions $\mathcal{P}=\bigsqcup_{n\geq 0} \mathcal{P}_{n}$ becomes a unital semigroup with the unit $1=\emptyset$ corresponding to the empty partition; we denote by $\mathbb{R}[\mathcal{P}]$ the corresponding semigroup algebra, the elements of which are formal linear combinations of partitions. blocks.title: Asymptotics
blocks.content:
In the current paper we consider asymptotic problems which correspond to the limit when the number of boxes $n\to\infty$ of the random Young diagrams tends to infinity. This corresponds to considering a *sequence* $(\chi_n)$ of reducible characters $\chi_n\colon \mathcal{P}_{n}\to\mathbb{R}$ and the resulting *sequence* $(\mathbb{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\chi_n})$ of probability measures on $\mathbb{Y}_{n}$.

We also allow that the deformation parameter $\alpha(n)$ depends on $n$; in order to make the notation light we will make this dependence implicit and write shortly $\alpha=\alpha(n)$.

blocks.title: Hypothesis: asymptotics of
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:hypothesis-double-scaling label="sec:hypothesis-double-scaling"} All results of the current paper will be based on the assumption that $\alpha=\alpha(n)$ is a sequence of positive numbers such that $$\label{eq:double-scaling-refined}
\frac{-\sqrt{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha}}}{\sqrt{n}} = 
g+ \frac{g'}{\sqrt{n}} + o\left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \right)$$ holds true for $n\to\infty$ for some constants $g$, $g'$.

Note that the most important case when $\alpha$ is constant fits into this framework with $g=0$. The generic case $g\neq 0$ will be referred to as *double scaling limit*.
